transcript.text: Our Samsung combi microwave keeps whirring for a few minutes after it's finished and beeped, even with the door open. Old one never did that. Is the fan stuck on?

It is highly unlikely that your fan is "stuck" in a broken sense. Instead, this behavior is almost certainly normal operation for modern Samsung combi microwaves.

Here’s why this happens and what you should know:

### 1. Cool-Down Cycle (Most Likely)
Modern combi microwaves (especially those with convection/grill functions) have powerful internal fans that cool down critical components like the magnetron, inverter, and control board after use. This is especially true if:
• You used the Grill or Convection function (these generate significant heat).
• The microwave was running for a long duration.
• Even with standard microwave-only cooking, high-power settings can trigger this.

The fan will continue to run until internal temperatures drop to safe levels, even if the door is open. This can last anywhere from 1 to 5 minutes after the beep stops.

### 2. Door Switch Logic
Some Samsung models are designed to keep the cooling fan running regardless of door position during this cool-down phase. The system prioritizes component protection over user convenience in this specific post-cycle window. Once temperatures normalize, the fan will stop automatically.

### 3. How to Confirm It’s Normal
• Check your manual: Look for a section on "Cooling Fan" or "Operation After Cooking." Most Samsung manuals explicitly state that the fan may run after cooking ends.
• Listen closely: The whirring should be consistent and not accompanied by grinding, clicking, or unusual vibrations (which would indicate a mechanical fault).
• Wait it out: If the fan stops on its own within 5–10 minutes of finishing, it’s definitely the cool-down cycle.

### When to Be Concerned
Contact Samsung support if:
• The fan runs for more than 10–15 minutes after cooking ends.
• You hear grinding, screeching, or rattling noises (not just a normal whir).
• The microwave feels excessively hot on the outside vents during this period.
• The fan never stops, even after extended idle time.

### Recommendation
1. Try using only Microwave mode next time and see if the fan still runs afterward. If it doesn’t, then the behavior is tied to higher-heat functions (Grill/Convection), which is normal.
2. Ensure vents are clear: Make sure nothing is blocking the intake or exhaust vents on the sides/back of the microwave. Restricted airflow can cause longer cool-down times.
3. Check for firmware updates: Occasionally, Samsung releases updates that adjust fan control logic. You may be able to check this via the SmartThings app if your model supports Wi-Fi.

Bottom line: This is almost certainly a designed safety feature, not a malfunction. Your old microwave likely had simpler cooling logic or no convection/grill function, which is why it didn’t exhibit this behavior.
